description: [S7.5, kind `measure`] A frame that rasterises TWO full terrain passes overruns the original's 87 ms frame in the app: the zoom keys (`X` / `Z`) gave two frames per session of 144..186 ms work (2 passes, 764,560 / 956,626 px), periods 148..191 ms, over three sessions (5_app_ingame_facts.json and 5_app_ingame_facts_lowload.json `pacing_over`). A frame with ONE full pass (a camera move with the arrow keys, 262,017..480,679 px) worked 35..75 ms and held 87 ms; a frame with no pass 4..7 ms. Two sessions ran while the PC was at 100 % CPU (12 logical processors) from other sessions' runs, the third with less load (the same course_season --live-trace took 72 s instead of 143 s), where the two frames still worked 149 / 176 ms; the sim thread runs at THREAD_PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL. The rasteriser (port/src/sim/gl_raster.cpp, S3's) was not profiled. The original's own cost for the same frames (Windows' generic GL in software) is not measured either.
path to resolution: Re-measure test_app_ingame.py::test_terrain_pass_frames_fit_the_frame (xfail, strict=False) on an idle PC; if it still overruns, S3 makes GlRaster faster (log/roadmap/S7/5_merge.md section 2) or the frame keeps the original's rule (no wait after an overrun, which the app already keeps)

description: [S7.5, kind `scope`] At this base (b3d61e41 + S3.2) the in-game frame the app shows holds the terrain and the HUD text only: the HUD panels, the radial toolbar at the bottom left, the build palettes and every sprite (trees, buildings, golfers, the ball, the flag) are not drawn, because the gfx backend has no body for them yet (framegate census of this mirror: 589 in-game rows UNSUPPORTED, 3 PASS; log/roadmap/S7/5_census_x64.tsv). The app presents what the backend draws and needs no change when S2 / S3 add the bodies. A player must click the toolbar blind (log/roadmap/S7/5_notes.md section 6 gives the positions).
path to resolution: S2's HUD / panel steps and S3.5 (sprites) add the bodies; re-run port/test/test_app_ingame.py, whose (2) judges every framegate in-game PASS row on the app path

description: [S7.5, kind `method`] In game the app presents the back buffer at H1's frame wait (LiveSession::wait_point, S7.6's design), but the original presents it earlier in the frame, at P6's display present slot [[0x0083ad50]+0x9c] (re/analysis/sim/mainLoop_structure.md row P6, call at 0x00418cd1). Whatever the frame draws into the back buffer between P6's present and H1's wait reaches the original's window only at the next frame's present, and the app's window at once. Not measured whether such drawing exists; framegate's checkpoints are the back buffer at the H1 wait too, so the gate does not see it.
path to resolution: Record the back buffer at P6's present call and at the H1 wait in one trace run (a tick hook point at P6's present, a tick.cpp change: S7 lead) and count the frames whose two buffers differ

description: [S7.5, kind `measure`] LiveTerrain keeps a log line for every Terrain call (terrain_live.cpp log_, for the recorder comparison) and never trims it, so a long play session grows memory with every call. session.json now reports `terrain_calls` (live sessions and --live-trace runs): course_season over --live-trace logged 25,671 calls in 6,296 frames (4.1 per frame, 5_bench2.log), about 158,000 lines per hour of play at 93 ms frames (38,700 frames); the bytes per line were not measured.
path to resolution: Measure the process's memory over a long session and, if it matters, ask S3 for an option that keeps no log in the app
